messages:
Alex: Heads up — latest deploy (merge b3f9a2c) introduced a perf regression on INT8 paths, seeing ~30-50% token latency increase on canary for long seqs. :grimacing:
Maya: saw the CI perf job fail this morning, perf/regression-int8 had a 42% regression vs baseline. failing job: https://ci/internal/1234
Devon: repro locally with the perf harness: `python tools/perf_run.py --model=/models/gpt-small-int8 --seq=1024 --batch=4` — I get the same spike.
Alex: attaching profiler summary I grabbed from the canary node: 
```
--- perf summary ---
kernel_select: 5%
dequantize: 48%
kvcache_lookup: 12%
attention_mt: 25%
other: 10%
end
```
Maya: dequantize at 48% is the smoking gun. Before the merge dequant was ~12%. Something changed in kernel selection pathway so we pick a slower dequant kernel for large seqs.
Devon: bisected to commit b3f9a2c (encoder: add dynamic kernel routing + heuristics) — that code prefers an "all-int8" kernel for throughput but accidentally routes long-seq requests to a codepath that dequantizes to FP32 on-host.
Sarah: that explains KV cache thrash too — when we dequant on host we lose KV cache memory layout optimizations, causing extra memcpy. Can you paste the bisect result?
Devon: paste: `git bisect log` -> found culprit b3f9a2c, commit message "dynamic kernel routing: prioritize int path for throughput"
Maya: Repro of mem-metrics shows GPU->CPU memcpy spikes: `nvidia-smi dmon shows memory transfer up 3x`
Alex: Immediate mitigation options: 1) revert b3f9a2c (fast) 2) hotfix runtime to prefer FP16 dequant kernel for seq>512 3) disable the new routing flag in canary config. Thoughts?
Sarah: I pushed a quick config flip to canary to disable new routing flag, canary latency dropped back ~10% but CI still shows regression on full suite.
Devon: I prototyped a smaller change: add guard to keep old kernel for quantized models when seq > 512 or batch_coalesce > 2. Patch reduces dequant time in perf harness by ~70%. Code snippet:
```
if model.is_quantized and seq_len > 512:
    select_kernel("legacy_int8_kv_fused")
else:
    select_kernel("dynamic_route_v2")
```
Maya: Could we ship that as a targeted rollback instead of full revert? less blast radius.
Alex: Agree. We should open a revert PR for b3f9a2c and a follow-up PR for the guard patch so we can reintroduce routing after tests. Devon, can you open the guard PR? I'll open the revert.
Devon: On it, will include perf numbers and unit test for kvcache layout invariants. Also running full evals for quality (we don't want regressions in output).
ci-bot: [perf/regression-int8] job queued — baseline comparison enabled.
Maya: note for on-call: if you see token-latency > 2.0s on canary route `int8-lower-lat`, switch traffic to fallback route `fp16-stable` (run `reconfigure route int8-lower-lat -> fp16-stable`).
Sarah: added a dashboard panel showing dequant time percentile and KV memcpy rate, dashboards/eng-runtime/dequant_kv_mem.json
Alex: Thanks team. Plan: 1) revert merge (short PR) 2) land Devon's guard patch + perf tests 3) run canary with guard then re-enable routing flag behind an experiment. I'll post PR links here when ready. :thumbsup:
Devon: PRs opened: revert -> https://git.internal/r/4321, guard -> https://git.internal/r/4322
Maya: monitoring the perf job, will report back when CI finishes.
ci-bot: [perf/regression-int8] completed: regression reduced to 3% after revert+guard on canary.
Alex: Excellent. We'll keep the revert until we add more kernel variants and better heuristics. Follow-ups: add automated perf test for seq lengths [128,512,1024] for quant models and a CI gate.
Sarah: Filed follow-up issues: ENG-987 (kernel variant coverage), ENG-988 (quant perf CI gate).
Maya: closing loop: alerting updated, rollback doc updated in runbooks/quant-regress.md
Alex: closing thread — thanks all.
